source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-80: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 80 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat the hang as an observation, not proof of cause. Assume the collective, tensor and message shapes, failing world sizes, placement, launcher, and software stack are reproducible; unknown platform facts must be measured. Record exact NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/container/launcher versions, node and GPU inventory, rank-to-device mapping and order, topology, parallel mapping, selected interface and NIC/NUMA affinity, MTU/routes, transport mode, rendezvous endpoint, firewall and authorized ports, timeout policy, and clock synchronization. Redact endpoints, tokens, and credentials.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 80: rank mapping or communicator order diverges when new ranks join. Hold workload, versions, placement, message sizes, and timeout policy constant. Capture synchronized per-rank logs with the last completed communicator phase/collective, rank mapping, selected transport, first-failure timestamp, and timeout reason. Binary-search the minimum failing world size. Run repeated matched trials varying one factor at a time: explicit rank mapping; an approved interface/NIC binding; topology-preserving placement; and a reduced-world control. For network hypotheses collect per-link bytes, drops, errors, retransmits, congestion, bandwidth in GB/s, latency in microseconds, and CPU/GPU/NIC utilization; for resource hypotheses collect limits, allocations, and open connections. Compare success rate, time-to-communicator (s), collective latency (ms), timeout rate, and rank skew (ms), with medians and p95/p99 over the same workload.

Interpretation: the hypothesis is supported only if the proposed factor changes the failure boundary and the matched control reproduces the effect; otherwise keep it unconfirmed and test the next factor. Do not claim an improvement from one run or correlated counters. Use read-only diagnostics first and least privilege. Pause and preserve logs if a timeout, data-integrity error, unexpected endpoint, elevated error/drop counter, or more than 1% regression in successful completion or p99 latency occurs. Roll back to the last known-good image/configuration, restore the prior rank/interface mapping, terminate only the owned job, and verify communicator cleanup, no orphan processes, and stable counters before retrying. Never broaden firewall rules or expose credentials merely to test reachability.
risks: correlated telemetry may not identify the causal mechanism
larger-world-size retries can consume cluster resources or leave stale communicators
network and endpoint diagnostics can expose sensitive infrastructure details
evidence_required: synchronized per-rank logs and communicator phase
exact versions, topology, rank mapping, interface/NIC affinity, and rendezvous/port configuration
matched repeated trials with reduced-world and one-factor controls
time-series network, resource, and collective metrics with units
rollback and cleanup verification
